newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC POWER THEIR WAY TO 2-1 SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC POWER THEIR WAY TO 2-1 SUCCESS.

text.p: Celtic closed the gap on Rangers to eight points at the top of the Scottish premier division when they won 2-1 at Heart of Midlothian on Saturday with Portugese striker Jorge Cadete scoring both goals.
Rangers will have a chance to re-establish their 11-point advantage in their quest for a ninth successive title when they play Aberdeen on Sunday.
But Scotland's match of the day was threatened by a power failure at Tynecastle which left the stands in total darkness and the electric turnstiles jammed shortly before kick-off.
It looked as though the match would be called off but engineers managed to restore the power and the game started 20 minutes later than scheduled.
Cadete opened the scoring after 28 minutes, Jim Hamilton equalised for the home side 10 minutes later before a superbly taken individual goal from Cadete (68th) secured the points for the visitors.
Dundee United moved three points clear of Hearts in third place by winning 3-1 at Dunfermline where striker Kjell Olafsson put them on the way to victory with goals in the 55th and 59th minutes.

United had Eric Pedersen sent off in the 63rd minute for a second booking. Harry Curran scored for Dunfermline five minutes from time before Jim McInally wrapped up the points for United with their third a minute from time.

At the other end of the table, bottom club Raith Rovers gave their chances of surviving relegation a boost, winning 1-0 at Kilmarnock who fell to second-bottom after Kevin Twaddle's 31st minute goal secured Raith's victory.
Motherwell climbed away from the bottom with a 2-1 win over Hibernian.
